scope: Independent source audit of directory-only retirement; not full empirical performance qualification or a formal verification of every accepted input.

resource_deltas.new_user_space_stack_state: bounded O(1), compiler/ABI-dependent; not measured as zero bytes

construction_work.root_iteration: O(CLI_MTARGETS), a fixed existing target count
construction_work.pattern_eligibility_check: O(total logical rules) worst case, one pointer/null/macro-pointer test per visited rule; can return early
construction_work.directory_reclaim: constant user-space metadata work and at most one madvise per retired fragment; kernel work may depend on advised page count
construction_work.old_whole_pool_flush: unchanged location before bytecode preparation; no second full free-list traversal

runtime_ownership_findings: Candidate cleanup directory has no scanner reader; immutable linked candidate chains preserve their original object addresses/order.
The sole scanner pattern-directory access is in lsig_sub_matched macro handling; every root with any macro_ptids or unknown logical metadata retains that table.
cl_load rejects loading a DB once CL_DB_COMPILED is set.
Retirement is restricted to engine-owned pool roots after bytecode succeeds; cl_engine_free destroys that pool after resource cleanup.
No-pool and standalone/regex matchers retain their original cleanup behavior.
important_limits: The engine pool is not globally read-only: existing clean-result cache entries are mutated under their existing locks.

Fixed-configuration scan bodies do not add engine-pool allocation sites, but public setting mutation can allocate engine-pool strings or initialize a cache after compilation; no blanket post-compile-allocation-free claim.
Bytecode execution can create/allocate its own context-owned pool, distinct from engine->mempool; that behavior is unchanged.
Source equality establishes zero new scan resource mechanisms, not absolute scan scratch/context size or latency on all machines.
Compile eligibility adds O(logical rules) work and reclaim advice has a page-dependent kernel cost; startup/reload/update CPU and wall time must be measured.
Concurrent scanning requires the existing lifecycle: compile and retire before publication, hold engine references while scanning, destroy only after workers finish.

The public API does not explicitly document compile-twice semantics; the existing compact ac_pack_nodes path already consumes its build index. Retrying a successfully compiled engine is not newly proven safe by this audit.
Future upstream code adding another runtime directory reader must update the retirement eligibility rule and tests.
These observed hashes must match the final implementation; rerun the audit after any relevant source change.

pool_class_and_private_layout_identity.scope: both architecture size tables, pool/fragment structs, to_bits/from_bits and alignment functions before mpool_create
